weekly.headline: Windows gets an NVIDIA-powered agent layer, and CI becomes the gate
weekly.intro: Microsoft and NVIDIA put local AI agents at the centre of Windows while security teams drowned in machine-generated vulnerability reports they cannot triage.

themes.title: Copilot gets file and OS-level control on Windows
themes.takeaway: Copilot can now read local files and act across Windows, so endpoint policy, DLP and device standards need revisiting before the October 16 Surface launch.
themes.detail: At Microsoft's San Francisco event, Nadella and Jensen Huang announced co-engineered hardware and software for on-device agents, with the NVIDIA RTX Spark-based Surface Laptop Ultra shipping October 16 from $2,599 and similar machines from Dell, Lenovo, HP, MSI and Asus up to $7,000. Microsoft frames the model as 'Hybrid Intelligence', splitting work between local and cloud. Apple moved the opposite way the same week, tightening macOS Full Disk Access specifically because AI agents make broad file permissions riskier.

themes.title: AI-generated bug reports break disclosure workflows
themes.takeaway: Machine-generated findings now outpace human triage, so route vulnerability intake through automated evidence-based scoring rather than adding reviewers.
themes.detail: Google froze its open source bug bounty programme over a significant rise in AI submissions, and GitHub imposed limits on private vulnerability reporting accounts. HackerOne research shows remediation is getting faster while exposure debt grows faster still. AWS published a two-part guide to building an AI triage harness with a steering file enforcing structural verification and evidence-based scoring, alongside its Continuum autonomous code security work.

themes.takeaway: Your CI pipeline and code review are now the only controls on agent output, and both need hardening before agent throughput rises further.

GitHub is also rebuilding its Git infrastructure for 'agent-scale' development while running live.
